# API Client & Response Typing

* **No Hono RPC client.** `hc<AppType>` over ~140+ endpoints hung the editor's type checking; routes are plain unchained `app.route(...)` statements.
* **Generated paths.** `shared/config/api-routes.ts` is auto-generated (never hand-edit; regenerate with `corepack pnpm gen:api-endpoints` after any route change) from the mounted Hono `app.routes`, with query-param helpers drawn from `QUERY_CONFIG` in `shared/config/api.ts`. It exports `apiRoutes` and the `ApiEndpoint` type, with no Hono dependency, so `sanity/` can import it safely.
* **`apiFetch`** (`next/lib/api/next-api.ts`) wraps `fetch` with JSON/FormData handling, `credentials: 'include'` for the session cookie, and central error parsing (it throws an `ApiError` carrying the HTTP status); callers pass `apiRoutes.x.y(...)` into it. Per-domain wrappers live in `next/lib/api/*-api.ts`. Server-side reads that can be personalized forward the request cookie (`getRequestCookieHeader`) and go through `cachedUnlessPersonalized`: tagged Data Cache when anonymous, `no-store` when a cookie is forwarded.
* **No time-based revalidation.** Every cached read — `cachedPublicRead`, `cachedUnlessPersonalized` without a cookie, and the public-profile reads in `profile-api.ts` — is a `force-cache` Data Cache entry with tags and no `revalidate`, so it never expires on a clock. The only thing that refreshes one is tag invalidation: the Hono mutation calls `revalidateCacheTags`, which POSTs the affected tags to `/api/revalidate`. A mutation route that skips that call, or an invalidation that never reaches the deployment, leaves its entries serving the build-time body until the next successful invalidation. Sanity reads follow the same rule with a single `sanity` tag (`next/sanity/lib/utils.ts`), with the difference that nothing currently invalidates that tag: Sanity edits are meant to arrive with the next rebuild.
* **Typed responses.** Route response shapes live in `shared/types/` and are applied at the route (`c.json<LoginResponse>(...)`), so backend and consumers share one definition. Anything a `hono/` route imports must live under `shared/`, never `next/types/`. Request-side safety comes from runtime validation (`zValidator`, guards).
